pages.title: The Lines Under the Gauge
pages.text: The crucible lists what it holds. Metal rows are percentages of the **metal** in the bath, not of the whole volume, so a bronze that is correctly 90/10 reads as 90 and 10 even when a fifth of the bath is slag.$p$pThe Slag row is the odd one out: it is a share of the whole bath, because that is the number the clean limit is measured against.

pages.title: What Counts as Clean
pages.text: Below **2%** slag the bath is still the metal TFC names, and it pours clean - except the steels, which are held to **0.5%**, because ground-inclusions in steel are exactly what ruins an edge. Past the line the pour is Flawed: same alloy, same ratio, worse object.$p$pA melt whose ratio misses the band badly enough is not any alloy at all and comes out as junk, so aim at the band and skim the dirt off separately.

pages.title: Names Follow Heat
pages.text: A cold crucible is holding metal, not melt, so its label drops the word Molten once the bath falls under the metal's melting point. The same line changes back when you reheat it.
